notes.b: Pre-marriage courses give couples a structured chance to examine what married life involves before they commit.
points: Courses explain the expectations and realities of marriage, so couples test their assumptions about married life before the wedding.
Accord, an Irish marriage and relationship support organisation, provides pre-marriage courses for couples.
Topics covered include communication, conflict resolution, relationships, family planning, child-rearing, finance and the legal requirements of marriage.
Practical topics include buying a home and managing the household budget as a married couple.
Couples examine their own personal qualities, such as honesty and openness, and discuss issues that could harm the marriage.
Courses prepare couples to recognise problems such as addiction, including alcohol abuse, and to seek help early.
They encourage openness and honest communication between partners.
They give couples a forum to discuss shared expectations about roles, money, housing and having children.
They build the skills needed to resolve conflict before it damages the relationship.

notes.h: Other facilities and services for couples preparing for marriage
points: The registrar of the area receives the written notice of intention to marry at least three months before the wedding, inspects proposed venues and registers the marriage.
Religious bodies may offer preparation for couples before a religious wedding, and the couple should check the requirements of their own religion.
Schools contribute to marriage preparation: Home Economics and SPHE classes examine the roles and responsibilities of partners in marriage and the laws relating to marriage.
Co-educational schools help students develop healthy interpersonal relationships between boys and girls, which supports later marriage.

keyTerms.definition: A course that prepares couples for the expectations, realities and responsibilities of marriage before the wedding.
The process by which partners identify disagreements and reach a solution both can accept.
Decisions a couple makes about whether and when to have children, and how many to have.
A relationship between two people, based on how they communicate, cooperate and treat each other.
The beliefs each partner holds about the roles, responsibilities and outcomes of married life.
The registrar for the area where the wedding takes place, who receives the notice of intention to marry and registers the marriage.

factCards.term: Four topics covered in a pre-marriage course
factCards.definition: Communication, conflict resolution, family planning and finance, all of which affect how the marriage functions.
It encourages openness, lets couples discuss expectations, gives advice on housing, money, parenting and family planning, and helps them recognise problems such as addiction.

factCards.term: Role of schools in marriage preparation
factCards.definition: Home Economics and SPHE classes examine the roles and responsibilities of partners and the laws relating to marriage.

factCards.term: Irish provider of marriage preparation courses
factCards.definition: Accord, an Irish marriage and relationship support organisation.

questions.prompt: Name two facilities or services available to couples preparing for marriage in Ireland, and describe what each provides.
questions.model: Any two of the following, each described: pre-marriage courses, such as those offered by Accord, which explain the expectations and realities of marriage and give advice on finance, family planning and communication; the registrar of the area, who receives the written notice of intention to marry at least three months before the wedding, approves venues and registers the marriage; religious preparation offered by churches or other religious bodies before a religious wedding; school subjects such as Home Economics and SPHE, which examine the roles and responsibilities of partners and the laws relating to marriage.

questions.prompt: Explain how a pre-marriage course can help a couple prepare for married life, identifying the topics it covers and the problems it helps them to anticipate.
questions.model: Topics: the course covers communication, conflict resolution, relationships, family planning, child-rearing, finance, the legal requirements of marriage and buying a home. How it helps: it explains the expectations and realities of marriage, so the couple test their assumptions; it encourages openness and gives them a forum to discuss shared expectations about roles, money and children; it builds the skills to resolve conflict before it damages the relationship. Problems anticipated: couples examine their personal qualities, such as honesty, and discuss issues that could harm the marriage, including addiction and alcohol abuse, and learn to recognise them and seek help early.
